result: Confirmed a real, diagnosable daemon error: `mcporter daemon restart` timed out (Chrome relay discovery/45s readiness timeout), and `mcporter daemon start --foreground --log` surfaced the underlying cause as `BrokerError: Previous daemon retirement is unverified; inspect its transports before deliberate recovery` (code daemon_unresponsive). Inspecting MCPorter's own state file ($HOME/.mcporter/daemon/user.json) showed a recorded pid that `ps -p` confirmed was no longer running -- an unclean prior retirement of MCPorter's OWN daemon (not a live shared service). After backing up and clearing that stale state (user.json, user.sock), `mcporter daemon start` succeeded (new pid, socket present). HOWEVER (fix-round correction), the original `mcporter list context-mode` / `mcporter call context-mode.ctx_execute` that followed did NOT exercise the keep-alive daemon path: mcporter auto-imported context-mode as an ad hoc STDIO server from `~/.codex/config.toml`, and `mcporter daemon status` at that point still reported `servers: []` -- i.e. the daemon-recovery work (stale-pid diagnosis and clearing) and that successful call were unrelated; the call would have succeeded the same way even with the daemon fully broken, since it never touched the daemon's keep-alive registration. The corrected fix-round re-run isolates the keep-alive path specifically: `mcporter daemon restart` reset to a clean daemon state, `mcporter --config ~/codex-ecosystem/config/mcporter.json daemon status` confirmed `servers: []` beforehand, `mcporter --config ~/codex-ecosystem/config/mcporter.json list context-mode` then registered context-mode as a keep-alive view, `mcporter --config ... daemon status` afterward showed that view as a CONNECTED entry in `servers[]`, and `mcporter --config ~/codex-ecosystem/config/mcporter.json call context-mode.ctx_execute ...` returned the tool's actual output ('mcporter-bridge-fix-ok') while that keep-alive registration remained connected. This before/after daemon-status delta plus a successful call through the same `--config` is the evidence that was missing: it directly exercises the keep-alive bridge referenced by the original gap-13 error, not an unrelated ad hoc STDIO import.

verdict_impact.explanation: Establishes that the previously-referenced daemon error was a recoverable stale-state condition in MCPorter's own daemon, AND (after the fix-round correction) that the canonical keep-alive registration path to context-mode -- the one implicated by the original gap-13 error -- is itself functionally reachable end-to-end (registration confirmed via daemon status, then a real tool call while still registered). Does not establish that every daemon error MCPorter can hit is this same stale-state class, nor does it change any north-star verdict.

limitations: Only one specific daemon-error mode was diagnosed and recovered (stale local state from an unclean prior retirement, confirmed via a dead pid); other possible daemon failure modes (e.g. an actually-live conflicting process, permission issues, a genuinely broken build) were not exercised.

Manual clearing of the stale state file was necessary because no documented `--force` flag exists on `mcporter daemon restart`/`start`; this is a reasonable but non-upstream-scripted recovery path, backed up before deletion.

Only the context-mode server was exercised through the daemon/bridge; other MCP servers configured for mcporter were not tested here (the canonical config also declares ai-memory and socraticode, neither of which was listed or called, to avoid touching the live ai-memory server and to keep this check's footprint minimal).

A live Context Mode process belonging to a running Claude session was never touched, per the binding rule; the keep-alive context-mode process spawned by MCPorter's daemon during the fix-round re-run is a separate, newly-spawned process (its own pid, launched by MCPorter's own daemon from the canonical config) and was left registered under MCPorter's daemon after the check, matching normal keep-alive behavior rather than being torn down.
